primary.summary: Every authenticated HTML page request is redirected to /logout because the jwtPage auth condition mishandles operator precedence, so the logged-in admin never sees the / link with the Admin nav link.
primary.rootCause: In server/handlers/auth.handler.js authenticate() the redirect condition is `((!user && isStrict) || (user || isStrict && !user.verified) || (user && user.banned))`. Due to precedence, the second clause `(user || isStrict && !user.verified)` is simply `(user || (isStrict && !user.verified))`; when a valid JWT resolves a user (even a verified, non-banned admin), `user` is truthy and the condition is true, so for req.isHTML with redirect === 'page' (jwtPage) the handler immediately does res.redirect('/logout'), destroying the session. The intended logic is to redirect only when the user is not verified, i.e. the clause should be `(isStrict && !user.verified)` or `(user && !user.verified)`. Hence after login, GET / (and every page) returns 302 to /logout, the page shows 'Logged out. Redirecting to homepage...' and navigation renders 'Log in / Sign up' instead of 'Settings', so a[href=/admin] never exists.

evidence.detail: TC-092 trace: POST /api/auth/login → 200 (login OK), then GET / → 302, followed by GET /logout → 200 and GET / → 200; the browser ends on the logged-out homepage.
Page heading after login is 'Logged out. Redirecting to homepage...' and the nav contains 'Log in / Sign up' instead of 'Settings'; no a[href=/admin] in the navigation (E1 element not found).

server/handlers/auth.handler.js:30-46: redirect condition contains `(user || isStrict && !user.verified)`, which is always true when a user exists; jwtPage (line 86) passes isStrict=true, redirect='page', triggering res.redirect('/logout') at line 38.

Differences from reference: GET / status 200 → 302 and nav link 'Settings'/settings → 'Log in / Sign up'//login, consistent with a forced logout redirect rather than missing seed data (seedCheck ok, no incidents).

suggestedFix.description: Fix the redirect predicate so verified, non-banned users are not redirected: change the second clause from `(user || isStrict && !user.verified)` to `(isStrict && !user.verified)` (or equivalently `(user && !user.verified)`), keeping the banned check separate.
suggestedFix.patch:
--- server/handlers/auth.handler.js
+++ server/handlers/auth.handler.js
@@
       if (
         req.isHTML &&
         redirect &&
         ((!user && isStrict) ||
-        (user || isStrict && !user.verified) ||
+        (isStrict && !user.verified) ||
         (user && user.banned))
       ) {

primary.summary: A wrong operator in parseQuery makes the default list limit NaN, so GET /api/v2/links returns limit: null instead of 10.
primary.rootCause: The parseQuery helper computes `const limit = parseInt(req.query.limit) && 10;` (server/handlers/helpers.handler.js:78). When no `limit` query parameter is sent, `parseInt(undefined)` returns NaN, and due to short-circuit evaluation `NaN && 10` evaluates to NaN. req.context.limit is therefore NaN; JSON.stringify of NaN yields null, so `GET /api/v2/links` reports `limit: null` instead of 10. The same helper builds req.context for all paginated list handlers (links.handler.js:20, users.handler.js:65, domains.handler.js:116), which is why 16+ tests sharing these endpoints all show the same difference. The SQL query itself then passes NaN to .limit(params.limit) (link.queries.js:126), relying on the query builder to fall back.

evidence.detail: server/handlers/helpers.handler.js:78 `const limit = parseInt(req.query.limit) && 10;` — parseInt(undefined) is NaN, and NaN && 10 evaluates to NaN; the intended default requires `||`.
This run: GET /api/v2/links response for TC-026/028/030/031/035 has limit=null; the reference run has limit=10 in every case (requests for those tests carry no ?limit param).

All list handlers read the value set here: links.handler.js:20 `const { limit, skip } = req.context;`, echoed into the response at links.handler.js:36; the single faulty line in parseQuery explains all affected endpoints and tests.

suggestedFix.description: Replace && with || so the default of 10 applies when the query parameter is absent or unparsable.

primary.summary: The created link's expire_in is null even for a valid '1m' value because the link creation query never stores the sanitized expire_in value.
primary.rootCause: The validator correctly sanitizes '1m' into a UTC timestamp (server/handlers/validators.handler.js:64-79, customSanitizer value => utils.dateToUTC(addMilliseconds(new Date(), value))), and links.handler passes expire_in through. But server/queries/link.queries.js:217 inserts `expire_in: params.expire_in && null`, which evaluates to null whenever a value is provided, so the column is always written as null. Hence POST returns 201 with expire_in: null (confirmed in the lastResponse artifact) and E2 fails; the later admin GET returned no useful result in the difference record because the test aborted first at E2.

evidence.detail: POST /api/v2/links returned 201 with body containing expire_in: null for expire_in '1m'.
link.queries.js:217 `expire_in: params.expire_in && null` — any truthy value becomes null; the sanitized timestamp from validators.handler.js:79 is discarded.
validators.handler.js:64-79 accepts and sanitizes '1m' to a UTC datetime, so validation is fine; the loss happens in the insert.
REQ-021 requires expire_in like '1m' to be accepted; acceptance criteria point at the validator chain.
No incidents or health problems; data was isolated/restored before the test.

suggestedFix.description: Pass the sanitized value through in the create query: change `expire_in: params.expire_in && null` to `expire_in: params.expire_in || null` so the UTC timestamp is stored.
suggestedFix.patch:
--- a/server/queries/link.queries.js
+++ b/server/queries/link.queries.js
@@
-      expire_in: params.expire_in && null,
+      expire_in: params.expire_in || null,

primary.summary: DELETE /api/v2/links/:id always renders an HTML partial (link removed dialog) instead of returning the required JSON {message}, because the branch is gated by a hardcoded `if (true)` instead of `if (req.isHTML)`.
primary.rootCause: In the `remove` handler (server/handlers/links.handler.js:349-372), after the link is deleted the response is wrapped in `if (true)` at line 360, so every DELETE renders the HTML partial 'partials/links/dialog/delete_success' (with HX-Reswap/HX-Trigger headers) and returns. The JSON path sending {message: 'Link has been deleted successfully.'} (lines 369-371) is unreachable dead code. Every other handler in this file (get, create, edit, report) branches on `req.isHTML`; it should be the same here. The API client therefore receives the HTML fragment body, so `delBody.message` is undefined and E2 fails (E3 is never reached, so the search request was not sent). The link itself WAS deleted correctly.

evidence.detail: DELETE /api/v2/links/dd80d710-... returned status 200 but its body is HTML: '<div class=content>...Your link ... has been deleted...' not JSON, so body.message is undefined.

server/handlers/links.handler.js:360 uses `if (true)` to unconditionally render 'partials/links/dialog/delete_success'; lines 369-371 send the required JSON message but are unreachable. Other handlers (e.g. report at 379, create at 149) use `req.isHTML`.
REQ-034 acceptance criterion: DELETE on own link returns 200 {message: 'Link has been deleted successfully.'} and the link no longer appears in GET /api/v2/links.

suggestedFix.description: Replace `if (true)` in the remove handler with `if (req.isHTML)` so HTML rendering only happens for HTMX/browser requests and the API gets the JSON response.
